answer: Resist sybils with an adaptive entry-difficulty ratchet: whenever the network sees a surge of new identities, the cost of entry — stake, delay, and fresh work — automatically ratchets upward for every newcomer, like a knoll that grows steeper the more climbers crowd it. A single thread of honest registration costs little, but each fake an attacker mints raises the price of the next, so ten thousand fakes face a ripple of escalating fees no one can outrun. Honest agents enter once at the low rate; forgers pay the ratchet they created.
